Hannah — thanks again for the demo this morning. FinServeOps is enthusiastic and we'd like to move forward with a pilot. Procurement asked me to get the DPA executed before we spin up test traffic. Attached is our standard DPA (FinServe_DPA_v1.pdf). Two items the GC is flagging up front:

Linda — great to hear, and glad the demo resonated. I'm attaching our redlines to your DPA (Redwood_DPA_redlines_v4.docx) and a current subprocessor inventory (subprocessors_inventory_20270601.csv). A few quick notes: 

- Subprocessors: we publish an inventory and can provide SOC 2 Type II reports for the infra vendors (cloud provider and storage layers). I attached the inventory and will secure the SOC 2 snapshots for the specific subprocessors you call out.
- KMS: for Redwood Hosted we do not expose HSM keys to customers today. For Dedicated or Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and can discuss a scoped offering for your pilot. For hosted pilot traffic we can commit to encrypting data at rest and in transit, and to enabling additional audit logging for the FinServeOps account.

If procurement needs a contractual commitment for notifications about new subprocessors, we can add a 30-day notification clause. If your GC insists on HSM for the pilot, that will require an exception and likely push the timeline.

Hannah / Monica — quick summary from Security:

- SOC2: we can produce the most recent SOC 2 Type II reports for our infra and platform subprocessors (cloud provider, storage provider). Those will be redacted for customer-identifying details but will demonstrate control coverage. We will prepare an export package by EOD tomorrow.
- Transfers: Redwood supports SCCs for EU-origin data. For Hosted accounts we do not currently guarantee EU-only physical processing by default, but we can (1) operate the pilot in the Frankfurt region to keep data residency in the EU and (2) apply SCCs contractually.
- KMS/HSM: we do not expose HSM-managed keys in Hosted. Dedicated/Private supports BYOK/HSM. Granting HSM access for a hosted pilot is operationally invasive and requires product/legal sign-off.

Risk/ask: offer a narrowly scoped commercial exception to allow the pilot to proceed: 1) commit to providing SOC2 artifacts within 72 hours; 2) operate the pilot in the EU region; 3) add a 30-day prior notice clause for new subprocessors; 4) a follow-up technical review within 90 days to revisit KMS needs.

I think this construct balances the customer's timeline and our controls posture. Monica — if Legal can sign off on the exception language limited to the FinServeOps pilot (deal FSO-2027-03-01), we can ask them to complete the DocuSign envelope.

-Vivek
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
